name: Guo Wu Guan (過五關)
description: Guo Wu Guan (過五關), meaning 'Passing Five Levels', is a Chinese domino solitaire game played with a standard set of 32 Chinese dominoes. The name alludes to the phrase 'Pass five levels and cut six generals' from the Three Kingdoms novel, featuring Guan Yu. Players must strategically remove valid triplets of tiles to clear five levels and defeat six generals.

history.origins: Based on the famous story from the Three Kingdoms period where Guan Yu 'passed five levels and cut six generals' while searching for his sworn brother Liu Bei.
timeline: Three Kingdoms Period (220-280 AD): Story of Guan Yu's journey becomes legendary.
Modern Era: Guo Wu Guan emerges as a solitaire game inspired by this legend.
history.cultural: Represents Chinese cultural heritage, combining dominoes with historical storytelling.
history.evolution: The game translates the narrative of Guan Yu's heroic journey into a domino puzzle.

setup.dealing: dealt, leaving a common row of 12 pieces, which are stored face down at the top of the layout.

rules.objective: Pass all five levels and cut all six generals by removing valid triplets of tiles.
rules.gameplay:
1. **Remove from Levels**: Find three adjacent tiles in any level that form a valid triplet. Remove them and add them to the left of the Common Row.
2. **Cut Generals**: When a level has only 1 tile left, use it with the two rightmost tiles from the Common Row to form a valid triplet. If valid, remove all three and flip the next General face-up.
3. **Critical Move**: Exactly ONCE in the game, you must use a single-tile level to cut TWO generals simultaneously (using the rightmost Common Row tile and the two rightmost Generals).
4. **Winning**: Win by clearing all levels and cutting all six generals.
5. **Losing**: Lose if the Common Row is empty and no valid triplet can be removed from any level.

strategy.basic: Plan ahead to ensure you can form valid triplets. Don't remove tiles randomly.
strategy.intermediate: Save the 'critical move' (cutting two generals with one level tile) for when it's most advantageous.
strategy.advanced: Work backwards from the endgame. Ensure you can cut the final generals with the tiles you'll have available.
tips: The critical move is mandatory—you must use it exactly once.
Track which tiles are duplicated to anticipate future triplet possibilities.

variations.name: Lenient triplets
variations.description: Tiles removed from a level in step 1 do not need to be adjacent; any set of three tiles in a level that form a valid triplet can be moved to the left end of the common row.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule change only; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: O-Koan (Wu Guan without generals)
variations.description: Five levels of four pieces; common row of 12 stored face down at top. No generals. Remove valid triplets from levels; replenish from common row. Repeat until all levels empty (win) or common row empty with no valid triplet (lose).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Different layout and no generals; full rule set differs.

variations.name: 通五关 (Tong Wu Guan)
variations.description: Similar to O-Koan but begins with 6 pieces in each level and 2 pieces in the common row.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Layout and deal differ; no single constant override.

variations.name: 七擒孟获 (Seven captures of Meng Huo)
variations.description: Single general tile 1-2 (Meng Huo), seven levels with 3 pieces each, common row of 10. General must be captured 7 times to clear all rows and win.

scoring.description: No point score. Win by passing all five levels and cutting all six generals; lose if the common row is empty and no valid triplet can be removed.
scoring.winCondition: Pass all five levels and cut all six generals. The game is lost if the common row is empty and there is no valid triplet of adjacent tiles in any remaining level.
